name: For Love Eternal
label: Quest
description: In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to free Anaya Dawnrunner's spirit from torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has endured since the city's fall.

clips.title: The story
paras: In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to free Anaya Dawnrunner's spirit from torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has endured since the city's fall.

Ten thousand years ago, the War of the Ancients tore ancient Kalimdor apart around the Well of Eternity. The catastrophe destroyed Ameth'Aran and took Anaya Dawnrunner from Cerellean Whiteclaw. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the druids' long hibernation. He hoped that walking the Emerald Dream through the ages would quiet his aching heart, but sorrow remained with him.

After awakening, Cerellean wandered Darkshore in a stupor until he reached Ameth'Aran's melancholy ruins. Among the ancient stones, he saw Anaya's tortured ghost. He cannot raise a weapon against the woman he loved, so he asks passing travelers to destroy her tormented form, retrieve her pendant, and grant her troubled soul peace.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: In the aftermath of the battles at the Well of Eternity, I heard that Ameth'Aran had been destroyed, its people dead, including my love, Anaya.

I would never have thought, thousands of years later, that memories of Anaya would still haunt my dreams. Wandering the woods of Darkshore in a stupor, I found myself in the ruins of Ameth'Aran... Where I saw the haunted spirit of my beloved.
She must be freed, but I lack the heart to do it. Her spirit must be destroyed.

clips.title: Progress
paras: With a great sorrow in my heart, I followed the Shan'do Stormrage into hibernation, and took my sorrow to my dreams, sleeping for the passing of thousands of years.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Thank you, friend. Perhaps it would have been better... If I had done it myself. But even after these thousands of years, I could not bear to raise my hand against my beloved.
Please, I would be alone with my grief...
